newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Ministers fail to agree fish satellite system.
newsitem.headline: Ministers fail to agree fish satellite system.

text.p: Fisheries ministers failed on Monday to strike a political agreement on a satellite system for monitoring fishing vessels.
The main difficulty was over the size of vessels to be tracked by satellites, Irish Marine Minister Sean Barrett told a news conference.

The Commission had proposed that vessels of more than 18 metres overall length be covered. In response to member state demands the Irish EU Presidency put forward a compromise of 24 metres but failed to gain the necessary support.
EU officials said this would more than halve the number of vessels covered to 4,000, from 9,000.
Fisheries Commissioner Emma Bonino said that another move to exclude vessels fishing for under 72 hours was even more difficult to accept.
Barrett welcomed the Commission's proposal to fund up to the entire capital investment cost of installing equipment on board, the so-called blue boxes, and fishing monitoring centres.
The Commission had proposed in 1993 to start the system for vessels fishing in non-EU waters, industrial fishing and driftnets over one km in length from January 1997.
The system would be extended to all vessels with an overall length of more than 18 metres from January 1999.
Several member states said the start-up dates should be delayed as the practical details still have to be defined.
Under the system, satellites will track vessel movements and transmit the information to their home countries which will then pass it onto the country in whose waters they are fishing.
Pilot projects between July 1994 and December 1995 showed that satellites considerably strengthened fishing controls, the Commission said.
